message.abstract: Due to the irreversible oxidation and leaching of the Ru catalytic center in acidic media, achieving a dynamic activity-stability balance of active sites based on static structural design is a paradox for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Here, we propose that the dynamic dissolution-deposition equilibrium of Ru sites governs the activity-stability trade-off of Ru-based oxides, which is engendered by Co, Zn-driven double-anchoring of Ru. It has been established that Co/Zn as electron donors not only inhibit oxidation of Ru and shorten Ru-O bond (first anchoring), but also attract the dissolved Ru species through oriented electron flow to achieve catalytic redeposition (second anchoring). Co, Zn co-doped RuO2 (CoxZn1−x@RuO2) with different Co ratios are constructed, in which Co0.8Zn0.2@RuO2 reaches the optimal dissolution-deposition equilibrium and displays no degradation either at 10 mA cm− 2 for 100 h or at 100 mA cm− 2 for 170 h, demonstrating excellent resistance to harsh OER conditions. Moreover, Co0.2Zn0.8@RuO2 exhibited ultra-high OER activity with 150 mV at 10 mA cm− 2 by tailoring the d-band center of Ru and lowering the energy barrier for *OOH adsorption.
title: Dynamic Ru equilibrium based on Co, Zn-driven double anchoring for robust acidic water oxidation
